excerpt: Verto (VertoFX) is a London-registered B2B cross-border payments platform with multi-currency accounts, FX and cards, built for businesses trading with emerging markets. Pricing, funding and alternatives.
content:
Verto, which started out as VertoFX, is a cross-border payments company for businesses. It gives companies a multi-currency account, lets them collect money from abroad, convert between currencies and pay suppliers in other countries, and offers a corporate card that spends in more than 160 currencies. A product called Verto Atlas lets other platforms embed these payments through an API. Its website lists startups, mid-size companies and enterprises as customers, with pages for exporters, importers, marketplaces, logistics firms, NGOs and education providers.

TechCrunch reported in September 2021 that Verto was founded in 2018 by Ola Oyetayo (CEO) and Anthony Oduwole (CTO), two UK-based Nigerians, and that it went through Y Combinator. It began as a marketplace for swapping hard-to-trade emerging-market currencies, such as the Nigerian naira, into major currencies, before adding a fuller payments suite. At the time it had more than 2,000 business customers and had just closed a $10 million Series A led by Quona Capital, after a $2 million seed round.

Verto's website says its UK entity, VertoFX Ltd, is authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority as an electronic money institution (firm reference 901073), and that its US business runs through a partnership with Global Innovations Bank. It also shows regulatory marks for Canada, Nigeria, South Africa, Kenya, Dubai and Tanzania, and claims ISO 27001 certification.

Pricing is published. When we checked, there was a free plan, Lite at $50 a month, Emerging at $100 a month and a custom Enterprise plan. Holding money and local payments are free on all plans; currency conversion costs 0.4% to 0.6% for major currencies and up to 2% for exotic ones, depending on plan, and SWIFT payments cost $20.

This page is research, not a review. We have not opened a Verto account; facts come from Verto's pages and the reporting under Sources.

faq.q: Is VertoFX the same as Verto?
faq.a: Yes. The company now trades as Verto; its UK entity is still VertoFX Ltd.
Its site says VertoFX Ltd is authorised by the UK Financial Conduct Authority under the Electronic Money Regulations 2011, firm reference 901073.
There is a free plan, Lite at $50 a month, Emerging at $100 a month and custom Enterprise pricing, plus per-transaction FX and payment fees.
Ola Oyetayo and Anthony Oduwole founded it in 2018, according to TechCrunch.

sources.label: TechCrunch: VertoFX picks up $10M for cross-border payments in emerging markets
